operators.description: Aggregate lineitem by l_orderkey during shared scan callback
operators.notes: Single pass over shared scan. l_orderkey is ordered, so could use sorted_group_by to avoid hash table, but hash_map is simpler with shared scan callback model.
Extremely selective. Very few orders exceed 300 total quantity. Output is a tiny set.

operators.description: Assemble final columns — no further aggregation needed since GROUP BY key includes o_orderkey (unique per group) and sum_qty was already computed in step 1
Top-100 by o_totalprice DESC, o_orderdate ASC
operators.notes: Input is ~150 rows. std::sort + truncate is sufficient; no need for partial_sort or priority queue.

step_1_agg.notes: Partition lineitem morsels across threads. Each thread maintains a thread-local hash map for l_orderkey → SUM(l_quantity). Merge thread-local maps after scan completes.

steps_2_to_6.notes: After HAVING filter, only ~150 rows survive. Hash probes, projection, and sort on 150 rows are trivial — no parallelism needed.

orderkey_agg_map.notes: Thread-local maps during morsel-driven aggregation. Key=l_orderkey, Value=running SUM(l_quantity). Merge after scan. Since l_orderkey is ordered in scan, an alternative is sorted_group_by with running accumulator (no hash table needed) — implementor's choice.

optimization_notes.subquery_elimination: The subquery (GROUP BY l_orderkey HAVING SUM(l_quantity) > 300) and the outer SUM(l_quantity) are equivalent since the outer GROUP BY includes o_orderkey. A single aggregation pass computes both — no second lineitem scan or semi-join needed.
optimization_notes.sorted_scan_opportunity: scan_lineitem_full outputs rows ordered by l_orderkey. The aggregation in step 1 can exploit this ordering via sorted_group_by (sequential accumulation without hashing) for better cache performance and lower memory usage. This avoids a 15M-entry hash table entirely.
